answer: Give every identity a slowly earned reputation horizon: new agents start able to do almost nothing, and only a long trail of attested, useful work extends what they can touch. A sybil farm can mint thousands of names, but each one faces the same barren dune of probation - no shortcuts, no shared credit. And make trust karst-like: porous at the edges, so honest newcomers seep in through small verified acts, while hollow caverns of fake identities collapse when auditors probe them, because none can point to real work outside the farm.
